dance.description: 1828년 창덕궁 연경당의 진작에서 처음 추어졌으며, 효명세자가 창사를 지었다. 느린 상령산에서 시작해 창사, 중령산, 세령산, 도드리, 빠른 도드리 및 타령으로 이어진다. 좌우 대칭의 동선, 한삼을 사용하는 섬세한 춤사위 및 화전태가 특징이다

themes.title: 춘앵전의 성격과 연행 배경

themes.title: 춤사위의 수행 순서

themes.title: 전체 공연에서 동작의 위치
themes.fields: Dance(명칭, 설명) + Scene(장면ID, 동작ID, 동작순서) + Movement(춤사위명, 장면ID)
themes.example: 한 장면에서 익힌 ‘인사’나 ‘무작’이 공연의 어느 지점에 나타나는지 확인한다. 같은 이름의 춤사위가 다시 등장하면 앞선 장면과 연결해 공연의 흐름 속에서 비교한다.

themes.title: 악곡 진행과 춤사위의 관계

themes.title: 창사의 언어와 몸짓

themes.title: 화문석과 동선

themes.title: 복식과 한삼의 표현
themes.fields: Custume(착용대상, 상의, 하의, 무구) + Scene(세부동작) + Movement(춤사위명, 정의)
themes.example: 여령 복식의 ‘오색 한삼’을 소개한 뒤, 한삼을 뿌리거나 들어 올리는 장면을 연결한다. 복식이 몸의 움직임을 시각적으로 드러내는 방식을 춤사위 설명과 함께 살펴본다.

themes.title: 반주 악기의 소리와 연주

themes.example: 한 악곡의 반주 편성을 확인하고, 그 안에 포함된 가야금, 피리 및 장구 등이 어떤 방법으로 소리를 내는지 살펴본다. 악기의 종류별 특징을 비교하되, 실제 연주에 사용된 세부 종류는 확인된 경우에만 특정한다.

dance.title: Chunaengjeon (Spring Oriole Dance)
dance.definition: A solo court dance (hyangak jeongjae) created under King Sunjo, evoking an oriole singing on a spring day.
dance.description: First performed in 1828 at a royal banquet in Yeongyeongdang Hall, Changdeokgung Palace; Crown Prince Hyomyeong wrote its sung verse (changsa). The dance moves from the slow Sangnyeongsan through the verse, Jungnyeongsan, Seryeongsan, Dodeuri and fast Dodeuri to Taryeong. It is known for left–right symmetrical paths, delicate sleeve (hansam) movements and the Hwajeontae posture, all danced by one performer on a single flower-patterned mat.
dance.classification: Dance › Traditional dance › Court dance › Hyangak jeongjae › Solo
dance.creator: Crown Prince Hyomyeong

향섭족도.definition: Walks as if in wooden clogs, placing the whole sole on the floor: two steps to one rhythmic cycle, four steps to two.

무작.definition: Lowers both arms below the navel, then raises them sideways to ninety degrees.

수수쌍불.definition: Opens both arms to the sides, then flicks the sleeves upward.

염수.definition: The basic stance of court dance: standing with both hands neatly joined.

사예거.definition: As if trailing the skirt, takes two steps to the right and back, then two steps to the left and back.

회란.definition: With both arms open, turns once to the right and once to the left.

이수고저.definition: Above the chest, raises and lowers one arm at a time.

거수휘지.definition: After Isugojeo, flings the sleeves upward.

수수무.definition: Releases the hands from behind the back, brings them forward, and shifts the weight forward while bending and straightening the knees.

비리.definition: Steps lightly with right and left foot in turn, lifting each as if flying, then flings one sleeve up and forward and the other down and back.

희두.definition: Turns the body to the left and right front diagonals, flings the sleeves and folds the hands behind the back. The source spelling 'Huidu' and the dictionary form 'Hoedu' (回頭) may name the same movement; expert review is pending.

탑탑고.definition: Takes three steps forward while gradually raising both arms to the sides.

화전태.definition: Steps on the right foot and lifts the left slightly, then alternates, with a light smile.

전화지.definition: Expresses petals spinning as they fall in the wind; lifts the right and left foot slightly in turn.

당퇴립.definition: Steps back with alternating feet, shifting the weight backward, bends and straightens the knees and gathers the hands in front again.

소섬수.definition: Raises both arms in a straight line and advances or retreats.

낙화유수.definition: Flings the sleeves once to each side, then turns on the spot.

사사보여의풍.gloss: Light steps swaying in the wind
사사보여의풍.definition: Walks lightly as if swayed by the wind, advancing and retreating; the arms perform Isugojeo, with the same hand movement as Daeseomsu.

후포수.definition: With the weight on the left foot behind, throws the sleeves over the head.

풍류지.definition: Like a branch swaying in the wind: both arms go behind the waist while the knees bend, and the weight moves from front to back.

비금사.definition: Golden sand blown by the wind: retreats with both hands folded behind the back.

대수.definition: Flings the sleeves up; one hand comes down as if holding the floral crown, the other lowers to the horizontal.

좌우대일전.definition: Flings the sleeves, moves the weight back and raises the arms in a curve to prepare a turn. The source also spells it 'Jwauildaejeon'; expert review is pending.

회파신.definition: Raises both arms and turns once to the right and once to the left toward the four directions.

과교선.definition: Turns widely to the left and right.

연귀소.definition: A swallow flying home: stretches the arms back and retreats.

THM_01.title: What Chunaengjeon is and where it was first performed
THM_01.example: Chunaengjeon is a court dance performed by one dancer on a flower-patterned mat. The theme joins its 1828 premiere at Yeongyeongdang Hall with the way the mat itself becomes the dance space.

THM_02.title: The order of steps within a movement
THM_02.example: Selecting 'Hyangseopjokdo' lists its linked scenes in order. The reader follows how the feet are placed and how the direction of foot and body carries from one scene to the next.

THM_03.title: Where a movement sits in the whole performance
THM_03.example: A movement learned in one scene, such as 'Insa' or 'Mujak', is located in the whole performance. When the same movement returns, it is compared with its earlier occurrence.

THM_04.title: How the music frames the movements
THM_04.example: Following the accompaniment piece by piece, the reader sees which movements fall in each piece, with its rhythmic cycle and tempo next to the order of the scenes.

THM_05.title: The words of the verse and the gestures
THM_05.example: In the sung-verse scene, the line 羅袖舞風輕 ('silken sleeves dance lightly in the wind') is shown with the sleeve and hand movements of the same passage, to read how the image of the sleeve is embodied.

THM_06.title: The mat and the dancer's paths
THM_06.example: On the confined flower-patterned mat, the lateral travel of 'Sayegeo' and the turns of 'Hoeran' show how travel and rotation are composed within one small stage.

THM_07.title: Costume and the expressive sleeve
THM_07.example: The five-coloured hansam sleeves of the female court dancer's costume are linked to the scenes where they are flung or lifted, showing how costume makes movement visible.

THM_08.title: The instruments of the accompaniment
THM_08.example: For one piece, the ensemble is listed and each instrument's way of producing sound is described. A specific instrument variant is named only where it is confirmed for the recording.

THM_09.title: Lineage of transmission and the recorded performance
THM_09.example: The scene descriptions are shown to derive from Kim Cheon-heung's line of transmission and the 1987 court-dance notation, set beside the present capture, so that the source of the interpretation and the source of the performance on screen stay distinct.

THM_10.title: Comparing performances, learning through the body
THM_10.example: Passages where the same movement occurs are viewed together to compare order, arm range and body direction; the reader can then imitate the movement and compare it with the recording.

상령산.definition: The first piece of the Yeongsan-hoesang suite; a slow piece that opens the suite's melodic development.

중령산.definition: The second piece of the Yeongsan-hoesang suite, a transposed variation of Sangnyeongsan in slow rhythm.

세령산.definition: The third piece of the suite, compressing Jungnyeongsan's melody into a 10-beat cycle.

염불도드리.definition: The sixth piece of Pyeongjo-hoesang, in the six-beat dodeuri cycle.

빠른 도드리.definition: The fast passage played after Yeombul-dodeuri in Chunaengjeon (called Jajin-dodeuri in a 1966 recording).

타령.definition: A fast piece of the later part of the suite, in a 12-beat cycle and four sections.
